name: Memgraph
tagline: In-memory, Cypher-compatible graph database in C++ for streaming and real-time graph workloads.
description: Memgraph is an in-memory property-graph database written in C++ that speaks Cypher over the Bolt protocol, so most Neo4j drivers and tools work against it unchanged. Data lives in RAM with snapshots and a write-ahead log for durability, which gives low-latency traversals and fast ingestion straight from Kafka or Pulsar streams. MAGE adds graph algorithms, and recent 3.x releases add vector and text search aimed at GraphRAG and agent memory. It is a strong fit when the working graph fits in memory and freshness matters; the community edition is source-available under BSL 1.1, with HA and fine-grained security in Enterprise.

license.name: Business Source License 1.1 (Community) / Memgraph Enterprise License

pricing.notes: Community edition is free to use under BSL 1.1; Enterprise (HA, RBAC, auditing) is priced by memory capacity.

scale.notes: The whole graph must fit in RAM of one instance; replication and HA (Enterprise) scale reads and availability, not size.

strengths: Low-latency traversals because the full graph is kept in RAM
Bolt and Cypher compatibility lets Neo4j drivers and many tools connect unchanged
Native Kafka, Redpanda and Pulsar stream ingestion with triggers for reactive graphs
Custom procedures in Python, C++ or Rust plus the MAGE algorithm library
Vector and text search built in for GraphRAG and agent-memory use cases
weaknesses: Dataset size is capped by RAM, which raises cost for large graphs
No sharding: one primary holds the entire graph
BSL licensing is not OSI open source and restricts offering it as a service
HA, RBAC and audit logs are Enterprise-only
useCases: Real-time fraud detection on streaming transactions
notIdealFor: Graphs much larger than available RAM
